topics: 🐐 Testing Rabbi Elazar's Rule — a female Paschal offering, before and after Pesach
🚫 Why a Guilt Offering's Offspring Never Gets Sacrificed Directly
📋 New Mishna: A Female Designated for a Guilt Offering
💰 Value-Sanctity Brings Inherent Sanctity Along With It
🔄 Rav Kahana vs. Rava — does consecrating a male 'for its value' still sanctify its body?

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Precisely When Does an Offspring Reach the Altar?
overview.subtitle: Temurah 19a–19b
overview.hebrewSource: מִיגּוֹ דְּנָחֲתָא לַהּ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים — נָחֲתָא נָמֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The Gemara pins down exactly when Rabbi Elazar allows an offspring itself to be sacrificed: only when its mother herself carried that same offering's status. This is tested against a female Paschal offering's offspring before and after Passover (when a leftover Paschal animal becomes a peace offering), and against a female designated for a guilt offering — which, since 'guilt offering' status can never attach to any female, means even Rabbi Elazar concedes the offspring cannot be sacrificed as one. A new mishna then addresses exactly this case, with Rabbi Shimon dissenting on whether the disqualified female must first develop an actual blemish before being sold. The underlying principle driving the majority view — that value-sanctity automatically drags inherent sanctity along with it — becomes the subject of its own amoraic dispute between Rav Kahana and Rava.

slides.title: 🐐 Before and After Pesach: When Does the Mother's Status Matter?
slides.subtitle: Rava and Abaye refine exactly what makes an offspring sacrifice-eligible

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: Rabbi Elazar only lets an offspring be sacrificed directly when its mother carries the SAME offering-status — like a female burnt offering, since a bird burnt offering can be female.

lines.speaker: Abaye challenges
lines.text: But a female Paschal offering that gives birth AFTER Pesach — when the mother becomes a peace offering — has its offspring sacrificed as a peace offering too, per Rabbi Elazar! Yet the mother was never 'peace offering' from the start!

lines.speaker: Rava responds
lines.text: After Pesach, the leftover Paschal animal genuinely BECOMES a peace offering — so the mother DOES carry peace-offering status by the time of birth. Before Pesach, no such status exists, so they'd disagree there too.

lines.speaker: Abaye's alternative
lines.text: Or: nobody disagrees before Pesach — 'wherever the leftover goes, the offspring goes too' is a fixed tradition. Before Pesach, mother and offspring are both consecrated only 'for value,' so neither is sacrificed directly.

callout.label: Ravina's resolution:
callout.text: The case must involve consecrating an ALREADY-pregnant animal — since a fetus is a separate 'body' (per Rabbi Yoḥanan), it can carry Paschal-offering status directly even while its mother carries only value-sanctity.

slides.title: 🚫 Why a Guilt Offering's Offspring Is Different
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yosei b'Rabbi Ḥanina pins down Rabbi Elazar's true logic

nodes.content: ❓ Does Rabbi Elazar's leniency (offspring sacrificed directly) ever apply to a female designated for a GUILT offering?
💬 Rabbi Yosei b'Rabbi Ḥanina: No — Rabbi Elazar concedes here to the Rabbis. Its offspring is NOT sacrificed as a guilt offering
🔑 Why not? Because a guilt offering can NEVER be brought from a female, unlike a burnt offering (which has a valid female bird form) — 'guilt offering' status can never attach to the mother at all
✅ This confirms Rabbi Elazar's rule is precisely about the mother's STATUS, not merely whether the offspring happens to be a valid male animal

callout.label: Why the teaching was needed:
callout.text: Without it, one might think Rabbi Elazar's leniency applies to ANY fit male offspring — the guilt-offering case proves it truly depends on the mother's own potential status.

slides.title: 📋 New Mishna: A Female Designated for a Guilt Offering
slides.subtitle: The Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon disagree on how it's sold
rows: Graze until an actual blemish appears, THEN sell it and buy a guilt offering
Even though unfit for its purpose, it still carries inherent sanctity that requires a genuine blemish before sale
If guilt offering already fulfilled otherwise
Proceeds go to communal gift offerings
The animal's specific purpose is now moot
May be sold WITHOUT waiting for a blemish
Its unfitness for the purpose (being female) already counts as equivalent to a blemish

callout.label: The deeper question:
callout.text: Does 'value-sanctity' (since it will be sold to fund an offering) automatically bring 'inherent sanctity' along with it, requiring a genuine physical blemish before sale? The Rabbis say yes; Rabbi Shimon says no.

slides.title: 💰 Two Theories of How Sanctity 'Descends'
slides.subtitle: Rav's principle vs. Rabbi Shimon's stricter fitness requirement

boxes.title: Rav's Principle (majority view)
items: Once value-sanctity (קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים) descends on an animal, inherent sanctity (קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף) automatically comes with it
Applies even to the female guilt-offering candidate — it needs a real blemish before sale
Rava: this even explains why a MALE consecrated 'for its value' still gets inherent sanctity and is fit to be sacrificed

boxes.title: Rabbi Shimon's Principle
items: Inherent sanctity attaches only to what is CURRENTLY fit for the altar
The female guilt-offering candidate is never fit — so no inherent sanctity, sellable immediately
Exception: an animal 'lacking only time' (מְחוּסַּר זְמַן, like a firstborn before 8 days) IS sanctified, since it's fit tomorrow — like a firstborn

callout.label: Precise limit of the exception:
callout.text: A guilt offering brought in the wrong YEAR (1st vs. 2nd) does NOT get the 'future fitness' exception, even though it will also be fit later — Rabbi Shimon's rule there is drawn specifically from the firstborn analogy, not simple future eligibility.

slides.title: 🔄 Rav Kahana vs. Rava — and Rava's Own Reversal
slides.subtitle: Does consecrating a male animal 'for its value' also confer inherent sanctity?

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rav Kahana: Yes — such a male becomes fully sanctified with inherent sanctity, since it IS fit to be sacrificed as the offering type intended
2️⃣ Rava (initially): No — designating it 'for its value' means only value-sanctity applies, nothing more
3️⃣ Rav Yehuda's citation of Rav settles it: value-sanctity always brings inherent sanctity with it, as a general principle
4️⃣ Rava retracts his own position and accepts Rav Kahana's view — a fit male consecrated 'for value' does carry inherent sanctity and may be sacrificed

callout.label: Why this matters for the mishna:
callout.text: This principle is exactly why the female guilt-offering candidate cannot simply be sold — even though she'll never be a guilt offering herself, her value-sanctity still pulls inherent sanctity in behind it.

summary.principle: Rabbi Elazar's leniency for a direct offspring depends entirely on whether the mother herself could ever carry that offering's status — which a female guilt-offering candidate never can — while the majority position holds that value-sanctity automatically brings inherent sanctity along, requiring an actual blemish before any such animal is sold.

flowSteps.content: 🐐 Rabbi Elazar's rule hinges on the mother's own potential status, tested via the Paschal-to-peace-offering transition
🚫 A guilt offering's offspring never qualifies, since no female can ever carry 'guilt offering' status

columns.content: 📋 New mishna: female guilt-offering candidate grazes until blemished (Rabbis) or is sold immediately (R' Shimon)
💰 Rav's principle: value-sanctity drags inherent sanctity with it — confirmed via Rava's retraction

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: sanctity that inheres in an animal's value is never merely monetary — it brings the animal's body under real consecrated status too

quiz.q: According to Rava's refined explanation, why does Rabbi Elazar rule that the offspring of a female Paschal offering IS sacrificed as a peace offering when born AFTER Passover, but not before?
o: There is no difference; Rabbi Elazar rules the same way in both cases
After Passover, the leftover Paschal animal itself becomes a peace offering, so the mother now carries peace-offering status which passes to the offspring
Peace offerings can only be female
The timing of Passover is irrelevant to this halakha
quiz.e: Rava explains that a leftover Paschal offering is reclassified as a peace offering after Passover, meaning the mother now carries that status — satisfying Rabbi Elazar's requirement that the mother herself carry the relevant offering-status.

quiz.q: Why does even Rabbi Elazar concede that the offspring of a female designated for a GUILT offering is never sacrificed directly as one?
o: Guilt offerings can never have offspring
A guilt offering can never be brought from a female animal, so 'guilt offering' status can never attach to the mother at all
Guilt offerings are always communal
Rabbi Elazar never discusses guilt offerings
quiz.e: Since a guilt offering requires a male animal, a female designated for one can never herself carry guilt-offering status — unlike a burnt offering, which has a valid female bird form — so Rabbi Elazar's leniency cannot apply here.

quiz.q: According to the new mishna, what does Rabbi Shimon rule about selling a female animal designated for a guilt offering?
o: It may never be sold
It may be sold without waiting for an actual physical blemish, since its unfitness for the purpose already counts as a blemish
It must always be sacrificed regardless of blemish
It must be given directly to the poor
quiz.e: Rabbi Shimon holds that being unfit for its designated purpose (female for a male-only offering) is itself equivalent to a blemish, so no additional physical blemish is required before selling it.

quiz.q: According to Rav's principle (cited by Rav Yehuda), what happens once value-sanctity (kedushat damim) descends on an animal?
o: Nothing further happens
Inherent sanctity (kedushat haguf) automatically descends on it as well
The animal becomes completely non-sacred
It can be redeemed immediately without restriction
quiz.e: Rav's principle, central to this daf, is that value-sanctity is never 'merely' monetary — it necessarily brings inherent bodily sanctity along with it, which is why the female guilt-offering candidate needs an actual blemish before sale.

quiz.q: What was the ultimate outcome of the dispute between Rav Kahana and Rava about consecrating a male animal 'for its value'?
o: Rav Kahana retracted and agreed with Rava
Rava retracted his own position and accepted Rav Kahana's view that such a male does carry inherent sanctity
They never reached any resolution
Both positions were rejected in favor of a third opinion
quiz.e: Rava initially held that such an animal carries only value-sanctity, but after hearing Rav's principle (via Rav Yehuda) that value-sanctity brings inherent sanctity with it, Rava retracted and agreed with Rav Kahana.
